nq1474755.title: Kempower Corporation Interim report 2026 1 January-30 September 2026: Outperforming a sharply weaker market, resetting costs for 2027
results: As investment in public charging slowed sharply, our order intake decreased by 19% and revenue by 10%.
Against this backdrop, our revenue grew 12% in January-September.
In Q3, while new public DC fast charging installations in Europe declined 22%, our European revenue declined 5%, and in Europe outside the Nordics it grew 10%.
In the Nordics, revenue decreased 30% as existing customers moderated investments.
Our revenue there declined 37% in Q3, but is up 32% from the beginning of the year.

outlook.text: The new outlook is as follows: 2026 revenue is expected to grow approximately 5% compared to year 2025, assuming no major impact from foreign currency exchange rates (revenue 2025: EUR 251.3 million). 2026 operative EBIT is expected to be lower compared to year 2025 (operative EBIT 2025: EUR -12.4 million).

Previous outlook: 2026 revenue is expected to grow between 10%–25% compared to year 2025, assuming no major impact from foreign currency exchange rates (revenue 2025: EUR 251.3 million). 2026 operative EBIT is expected to improve significantly compared to year 2025 (operative EBIT 2025: EUR -12.4 million).
The updated financial targets are: Revenue growth: 15-25% CAGR over 2025–2030, in constant currency, range based on different market growth scenarios.
With an order backlog of EUR 128 million (9% higher than a year ago) and liquidity of EUR 91 million, we have the backlog and balance sheet to deliver.

The division reported a total operating income of NOK 2 142 million, a reduction of 9 per cent compared to the third quarter last year, while EBITDA declined 43 per cent year -on-year.
The division reported total operating income of NOK 1 056 million, up 5 per cent compared to the third quarter last year, while the EBITDA increased 7 per cent year-on-year.

os685067.title: Navamedic ASA: Profitability improvement driven by product mix and cost discipline despite decreased revenue

The Adjusted EBITDA margin in the quarter was 8.8 per cent compared to 8.1 per cent in Q3 2025.
Revenues from Prescription Drugs were NOK 60.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to NOK 74.1 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Revenues from Hospital were NOK 32.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to NOK 29.5 million in the same quarter last year.

Underlying EBITDAC[1] amounted to negative NOK 1.7 million, corresponding to a margin of -1.0%, while EBIT was NOK 0.0 million, delivering an EBIT margin of 0.0%.

For the first nine months of 2026, revenue was NOK 593.0 million, compared with NOK 616.3 million in the prior-year period, a decline of 3.8% (a growth of 3.1% year-on-year, excluding currency effects of approximately NOK 42.4 million).
Revenue in the region grew 19.5% year-on-year, with the quarter's largest wins tied to the X20 Platform, including deployments at a major sports league that displaced incumbent infrastructure.

outlook.text: For 2026, Appear reaffirms its revenue guidance in the range of NOK 880--920 million, representing growth of approximately 10--15% year-on-year.
